name: OLED 128×32 0.91" (SSD1306, I2C)
description: 0.91" monochrome OLED, 128×32 pixels, Solomon Systech SSD1306 controller on I2C at address 0x3C, internal charge pump, on-board 3.3 V regulator so it runs from 3.3–5 V. Sold as: generic 0.91" 128x32 I2C OLED module (ProtoSupplies "OLED 0.91" 128x32 I2C White Display", HiLetgo, AZ-Delivery; 4-pin GND, VCC, SCL, SDA).
eli5: A thin little screen strip that shows four lines of text. It needs only 4 wires.
buildNotes: Check the pin order printed on the board: this module is GND, VCC, SCL, SDA; other OLEDs put VCC first.
Initialise for 32 rows: multiplex ratio A8h 1Fh and COM pins DAh 02h. The 128x64 setting (12h) gives broken, every-other-line text.
Enable the charge pump (8Dh 14h) before display on (AFh); nothing lights without it.
Only 4 lines of 8x8 text fit (y = 0, 8, 16, 24). Call show() after drawing.

driver.code:
# SSD1306 0.91" 128x32 I2C OLED, MicroPython driver.
# Command sequence from the Solomon Systech SSD1306 datasheet (Rev 1.1): section 10 command
# table and the charge-pump application note (8Dh 14h before AFh). A 128x32 panel uses
# multiplex ratio 31 (A8h 1Fh) and sequential COM pins without left/right remap (DAh 02h).
# I2C: control byte 0x80 = one command byte follows (Co=1, D/C#=0); 0x40 = data stream (Co=0, D/C#=1).
import framebuf
import time


class SSD1306_I2C(framebuf.FrameBuffer):
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x3C, width=128, height=32):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.pages = height // 8
        self.buffer = bytearray(self.pages * width)
        super().__init__(self.buffer, width, height, framebuf.MONO_VLSB)
        self.init_display()

    def cmd(self, c):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes((0x80, c)))

    def init_display(self):
        for c in (
            0xAE,                 # display off
            0xD5, 0x80,           # clock divide ratio / oscillator frequency (reset value)
            0xA8, self.height - 1,  # multiplex ratio: 31 for 32 rows
            0xD3, 0x00,           # display offset 0
            0x40,                 # display start line 0
            0x8D, 0x14,           # enable internal charge pump (module has no external VCC)
            0x20, 0x00,           # horizontal addressing mode
            0xA1,                 # segment remap: column 127 -> SEG0
            0xC8,                 # COM scan direction remapped (COM[N-1] -> COM0)
            0xDA, 0x02 if self.width > 2 * self.height else 0x12,  # COM pins: sequential, no remap for 128x32
            0x81, 0x8F,           # contrast
            0xD9, 0xF1,           # pre-charge: phase 1 = 1 DCLK, phase 2 = 15 DCLK (charge pump)
            0xDB, 0x30,           # VCOMH deselect level ~0.83 x VCC
            0xA4,                 # display follows RAM
            0xA6,                 # normal (not inverted)
            0xAF,                 # display on
        ):
            self.cmd(c)
        time.sleep_ms(100)        # datasheet: allow 100 ms after AFh for the panel to come up
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()

    def poweroff(self):
        self.cmd(0xAE)

    def poweron(self):
        self.cmd(0xAF)

    def contrast(self, value):
        self.cmd(0x81)
        self.cmd(value & 0xFF)

    def invert(self, on):
        self.cmd(0xA7 if on else 0xA6)

    def show(self):
        for c in (0x21, 0, self.width - 1, 0x22, 0, self.pages - 1):
            self.cmd(c)
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x40' + self.buffer)

# 0.91" OLED 128×32 (SSD1306 128x32)

## Overview
A tiny monochrome OLED strip, 128 × 32 pixels, driven by the Solomon Systech **SSD1306** controller over I2C. Hobbyists buy it as the generic **0.91" 128x32 I2C OLED module** (4-pin header: GND, VCC, SCL, SDA), sold by ProtoSupplies, HiLetgo, AZ-Delivery and many others. The board carries a 3.3 V regulator, so VCC takes 3.3 V or 5 V, and the SSD1306's internal charge pump makes the panel voltage.

## Pinout (generic 0.91" module, header order)
| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| GND | Ground |
| VCC | Supply, 3.3–5 V (on-board regulator) |
| SCL | I2C clock |
| SDA | I2C data |

## Electrical limits
- Module supply: 3.3–5 V. The SSD1306 logic itself is 1.65–3.3 V (VDD); the regulator on the module provides it.
- Current: roughly 5–20 mA depending on how many pixels are lit; budget 20 mA.
- I2C fast mode (400 kHz) works; the module's 4.7–10 kΩ pull-ups go to its own 3.3 V rail on most boards.

## Interface details
- **I2C address 0x3C** (SA0 low, fixed on most 0.91" modules; 0x3D would need SA0 high).
- Every write starts with a control byte: **0x80** = one command byte follows, **0x00** = command stream, **0x40** = data stream (GDDRAM bytes).
- 128×32 setup differs from 128×64: **multiplex ratio A8h 1Fh** (31 = 32 rows) and **COM pins DAh 02h** (sequential, no remap). Using the 128×64 value 12h gives every other line blank / stretched text.
- Charge pump: **8Dh 14h** before display on (AFh); the panel needs ~100 ms after AFh.
- RAM is 4 pages × 128 columns; each byte is a vertical strip of 8 pixels, LSB on top (framebuf MONO_VLSB).

## Wiring
- ESP32: VCC → 3V3, GND → GND, SDA → D21, SCL → D22.
- Pico: VCC → 3V3(OUT), GND → GND, SDA → GP4, SCL → GP5.
- Raspberry Pi 4: VCC → pin 1 (3.3 V), GND → pin 6, SDA → pin 3, SCL → pin 5.

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
from ssd1306_128x32 import SSD1306_I2C
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))
oled = SSD1306_I2C(i2c)          # 128x32 at 0x3C
oled.fill(0)
oled.text('Hello', 0, 0)         # 8x8 font: 4 lines of 16 characters
oled.show()
```
The stock MicroPython `ssd1306.py` also works: `SSD1306_I2C(128, 32, i2c)`.

## Gotchas
- **Check the header labels**: this module is GND-VCC-SCL-SDA, but some 0.96" boards are VCC-GND; a swap can kill it.
- Only 4 text lines (y = 0, 8, 16, 24) fit with the 8×8 font.
- Text looks squashed or every second line missing → driver initialised for 64 rows; pass height 32.
- Nothing shows but i2c.scan() finds 0x3C → `show()` was never called.

## Datasheet
https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/datasheets/SSD1306.pdf
